newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong handover police team to visit Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong handover police team to visit Beijing.

text.p: Hong Kong police responsible for security at ceremonies marking the British colony's return to China will visit Beijing to observe how their counterparts handle major events, a senior police officer said on Thursday.
But the eight officers going to Beijing will not discuss plans for security at the handover with Chinese officers, Dick Lee, Assistant Commissioner of Police (Special Duties), said by telephone.

The officers will visit in two groups as guests of China's Public Security Bureau for three to four days and will observe security measures and traffic control at two large-scale events in Beijing, Lee said. He declined to elaborate.
Hong Kong is bracing for a deluge of visitors, journalists and official guests in late June to witness the end of more than a century and a half of British colonial rule.
Hong Kong, which reverts to China at midnight on June 30, is planning lavish celebrations to mark the occasion and expects to host dignitaries from Beijing and London.
Noisy demonstrators have targeted Chinese officials visiting Hong Kong in the past year and police have described the protests as a security headache.
